# Results — Study 751 (Fortune-500-Inclusion)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The question — **"does making
(or falling off) the Fortune 500 move the stock, the way an S&P-500 index addition does?"** —
tested as a textbook short-window **event study**: around each dated **list-reveal**, the
**cumulative abnormal return** (CAR) is the stock's return minus a **market-model** fit
(`stock = α + β·SPY`) estimated on a clean pre-event window, cumulated over the event window.
Fortune sells no free point-in-time membership feed, so events come from a **hardcoded,
labelled, cited table** of ~26 notable debuts and exits (a **labelled proxy**, curated year).
Offline core + synthetic control are deterministic; run `python examples/verify.py` to
reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted closes — each event ticker + SPY (public, no key) |
| Event table | hardcoded `FORTUNE_EVENTS` (ticker, list-reveal date, added/dropped), fingerprint **9b280bbd9147** |
| As-of | 2026-07-12 |
| Window (cached) | 2015-01-02 → 2026-07-10 (event windows fall within it) |
| Events in table | **26**, all priced (**14 added / 12 dropped**) |
| Benchmark / model | market model `stock = α + β·SPY`, 120-day estimation window, 10-day gap |
| Event window | CAR **[0, +2]** trading days (canonical); robustness over [0,0], [−1,+1], [0,+4] |
| Entry / costs | tradable variant enters **1 day after** the reveal; one-way 10-bps round-trip |

> **Two named caveats (on the Signal axis).** (1) The debut/exit **year is a curated proxy** —
> a company's exact first (or last) appearance can be off by a year, and each is snapped to its
> list-reveal date. (2) **Survivorship**: the worst exits are *bankruptcies* whose series ends
> (J.C. Penney 2020; Bed Bath & Beyond 2023 — [`DELISTED_EXITS`](../fortune_500_inclusion/data.py)),
> biasing the surviving exit sample *against* a negative drop-reaction. Neither moves the
> verdict: it rests on a near-zero point estimate, an at-chance win-rate, and the **absent
> mechanism** — a Fortune-500 ranking forces no fund to buy and reveals no new information.

## Why this is *not* the S&P-500 index-inclusion trade

The real, documented index-inclusion effect (Study 249; Shleifer 1986; Harris & Gurel 1986)
has a **mechanism**: an S&P-500 addition forces **index funds to buy**, a genuine demand shock.
The Fortune 500 is a **media ranking by prior-year revenue** — no fund tracks it, no one is
forced to buy, and the revenue that decides the ranking was public months earlier. Strip out
the demand shock and the new information and only a **pure attention / prestige** effect
remains. This study tests whether prestige alone moves price. It does not.

## The signal — abnormal return around the list reveal (canonical CAR[0,+2])

| bucket | n | mean CAR | win-rate (CAR>0) | *t* vs 0 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **added** (debut on the list) | 14 | **+0.06%** | 50% | **+0.04** |
| **dropped** (fell off the list) | 12 | **+0.12%** | 50% | **+0.06** |
| all events | 26 | +0.09% | 50% | +0.07 |

**added − dropped = −0.06pp**, Welch ***t* = −0.02**, added-bucket placebo ***p* = 0.966**
(share of random same-size non-event windows on the same names whose mean CAR matches/beats
the added set). This is as close to a perfect null as an event study gets: both buckets sit at
**+0.1% with a coin-flip 50% win-rate**, the added−dropped gap is **−0.06pp** — statistically
zero — and a random draw beats the "added" pop **97%** of the time. There is no prestige pop,
no drop-off penalty, and no gap between them.

## The move that *would* have to exist — the announcement day — is also flat

Unlike a forced CEO ouster (Study 391), where the announcement *day* does jolt the stock,
here even the un-tradable [0,0] instant is dead:

| window | what it measures | added mean | *t* | added−dropped *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **[0, 0]** | the reveal-*day* repricing | **−0.47%** | **−0.56** | −0.12 | 0.556 |
| [0, +2] | a holdable 3-day window | +0.06% | +0.04 | −0.02 | 0.966 |

Even on the single reveal day the "added" names are **−0.47%** (placebo *p* = 0.56) — a
non-event. The Fortune 500 is announced with fanfare, and the tape does not blink.

## The tradable version — enter the day after, and there is nothing to enter

| trade | added mean CAR | *t* | added−dropped *t* | net @ 10 bps |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| enter **+1 day**, hold [+1,+3] | +0.88% | +0.60 | −0.22 | +0.78% |
| enter **+1 day**, hold [+1,+5] | +2.23% | +1.39 | +0.20 | +2.13% |

Widen the post-reveal window far enough and the "added" mean creeps to **+2.23%** — but at
**t = 1.39** it never clears the bar, the added−dropped gap is **+0.20** (noise), and this is
the single most favourable of several windows tried (window-mining). Costs are not even the
binding constraint; the signal is.

## Robustness — no window rescues it

| event window | added mean | *t* | dropped mean | added−dropped | diff *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| [0, 0] | −0.47% | −0.56 | −0.25% | −0.21pp | −0.12 |
| **[0, +2]** (canonical) | +0.06% | +0.04 | +0.12% | −0.06pp | −0.02 |
| [−1, +1] | −2.14% | −1.34 | −0.44% | −1.70pp | −0.75 |
| [0, +4] | +1.62% | +1.15 | +0.89% | +0.73pp | +0.27 |

Not one window crosses *t* = 2 on either bucket or on the difference. The point estimate even
flips sign with the window. This is what *no effect* looks like: the number is whatever the
noise in ~a dozen events per bucket happens to be.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful, small samples are weak

A deterministic per-event abnormal-return panel (14 added / 12 dropped) with a **plantable
added-bucket CAR edge**:

| planted added edge | added mean | added *t* | dropped mean | added−dropped *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0 bps** (no edge) | +0.49% | +0.48 | −0.90% | **+0.90** |
| **+500 bps** (large) | +5.49% | +5.40 | −0.90% | **+4.10** |

With **no** planted edge the added−dropped test stays below *t* = 2 (it cannot fake
significance from ~a dozen events per bucket). Only an **implausibly large** +5%/event planted
edge drives the difference to *t* = 4.1. The control proves both things at once: the engine
recovers a real effect when one exists, **and** a dozen-per-bucket sample is far too small to
detect a Fortune-500 attention edge of plausible size — which is exactly why the real-tape
*t* of ≈ 0 is uninformative *and* consistent with a true effect of zero.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The canonical CAR[0,+2] is **+0.06%** for adds (*t* = 0.04) and **+0.12%**
  for drops (*t* = 0.06), a **−0.06pp** gap at Welch *t* = −0.02 (placebo *p* = 0.97), with an
  exactly-coin-flip 50% win-rate in both buckets — and even the un-tradable reveal *day* is a
  flat −0.47%. No window clears *t* = 2. The one honest lens (a placebo null sized to the event
  count) says a random draw looks this "special" 97% of the time. Indistinguishable from noise.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** There is nothing to deploy: the most favourable of several
  windows (enter +1 day, hold five) reaches only **+2.23% at *t* = 1.39** before it is
  window-mined, the added−dropped spread is *t* = 0.20, and costs (not even binding) push it
  the wrong way. No edge at any size.
- **Attention effect? — NOT SUPPORTED.** The real index-inclusion effect (S&P 500) is driven
  by a **forced-buying demand shock** that a magazine ranking simply does not create — no fund
  tracks the Fortune 500 and the deciding revenue was already public. Absent the mechanism, the
  prestige/attention story has nothing to stand on, and the tape confirms it: zero, in every
  window, on both legs.
